title: One post, millions of feeds
summary: A post by a celebrity must reach millions of feeds; do it in the background.

steps.title: Write once, read once, or both
steps.text: When someone posts, followers must see it. Fan-out on write copies the post into every follower's feed now, so reading is fast. Fan-out on read leaves it alone and builds the feed when someone opens the app. Celebrities with 20 million followers make the first approach very heavy.

steps.prompt: A celebrity post makes 25 times the writes. Absorb it with a queue and workers.
steps.hint: Put a Queue and Worker pool on the write path so the copies are made in the background.

steps.title: A mix
steps.text: Big systems mix both: copy into feeds for everyday accounts, and for celebrities merge their latest posts in when the feed is read.

steps.why: The work is done at post time.

choices: Queues make every copy arrive faster
Copies must be made one at a time
The poster should not wait on copies
Queues are free, so they cost nothing
steps.why: The post is accepted at once and delivered over the next seconds.

steps.q: How do big feeds treat celebrities?
choices: Give each fan a private copy first
Merge their posts in at read time
steps.why: It avoids millions of writes per post.

takeaway: Do heavy fan-out in the background, and treat huge accounts differently.
